anya: quick sync—following up on the RFC about anchoring quant calibration to prompt cohorts. ran into a few ops edgecases during the canary

sam_t: saw that. which edgecases?

anya: mainly two: 1) long-tail prompts with repeated structure that blow up activation ranges, 2) per-head scale divergence when we do fp8->int8 heuristics

lee_ops: +1. on canary we saw a 2x latency spike for a subset of requests because batch padding changed shape distributions. logs: `WARN kv_cache: unexpected seq_len 512 on hotpath`

jordank: for (1) I think we need cohort-aware calibration: store separate min/max stats per cohort key and fall back to global if under-sampled. basically anchored histograms instead of single-run stats

maria_r: right, but storing per-cohort stats explodes metadata. suggested compromise: keep cohort fingerprints for top-1000 prompts and use a decay window for everything else

anya: here's a strawman config we piloted this morning:
```
precision_calibration: 
  tiers: [global, heavy_prompts, top_fingerprint]
  fingerprint_size: 1024
  decay_window_minutes: 60
  fallback_policy: {threshold_samples: 50, fallback_to: global}
```

lee_ops: that looks reasonable. runtime questions: how does runtime pick fingerprint? cheap hash of the first 64 bytes?

sam_t: we used a rolling murmur3 on tokens 0..15 to keep cost down. collisions are fine; heuristics tolerate a few mismatches

jordank: about (2) per-head scale divergence—did you see any correlation with layer type? attention vs feedforward?

anya: yes, attention heads were noisier on fp8 profiling, FFW stable. hypothesis: attention softmax amplifies small quant noise and scale drift across positions

maria_r: ops implication: when per-head variance > 0.2 we should either (A) apply headwise rescale before quant or (B) restrict to int8 for that layer. We need an API flag for contract: "precision_profile.overrides.layer.<name>.min_bitwidth"

lee_ops: +1 for API flag. Also need rollout safe guards. propose automatic canary that routes 1% of traffic to new profile, with auto-rollback if revenue-impacting metrics degrade

deploy-bot: deploy started: canary routing 1% -> profile: anchored-cohort-v1 at 2024-04-01T11:12:00Z

anya: operational checklist for the rollout: 
- ensure telemetry tags: profile_id, cohort_key, head_variance
- add alert: +10% latency or +3% token error rate -> auto rollback
- sampling trace: keep 10 random requests per minute with full trace for offline replays

sam_t: added a small telemetry patch to annotate logs: `telemetry.add({profile: "anchored-cohort-v1", cohort: fp_hash})`

jordank: interface boundary question: should the SDK expose cohort pins so SDK users can choose to opt-in to cohort-specific calibration? Or keep it internal only?

maria_r: exposing pins is powerful but dangerous—customers could overfit. prefer server-side only for first iteration, with an enterprise opt-in flag and docs

anya: agreed. add to product notes: "enterprise-only: cohort pinning and SLA guarantees for per-customer calibration"

lee_ops: one more runtime edgecase: when fallback to global happens mid-session, KV cache prefix mismatch can surface incorrect completions. we must surface a header `x-precision-fallback: true` and invalidate per-session cache when profile bitwidth changes

sam_t: good catch. we already have a cache-invalidate hook; will wire header->invalidate mapping

deploy-bot: canary metrics update: latency +1.8% overall, but a 12% tail in cohort "billing_table_parse". rollback recommended?

anya: let's pause the rollout for that cohort and open a short-term patch to force int8 for attention layers for that cohort. action items:
- sam_t: implement cohort-level override for layer bitwidth (ETA today)
- maria_r: document ops playbook and add `x-precision-fallback` header to the API contract (ETA EOD)
- lee_ops: add alert on cache invalidation mismatches (ETA tomorrow)
- jordank: run offline shadow eval on the billing_table_parse fingerprint and produce degradation report (ETA 24h)

jordank: ack, starting shadow eval now

anya: thanks team. one final note: long-term we want a unified precision-profile schema that supports anchored cohorts, headwise overrides, and a deterministic fallback tree. I'll sketch an RFC for schema v2 after we stabilize canary

sam_t: thanks—please tag me on the RFC draft.

maria_r: +1. also let's add a small sample notebook for ops to reproduce the billing_table_parse failure locally

anya: will do. closing the thread for now, reopening after the shadow eval results. :eyes:
